learningObjectives: Select and justify delayed service-level agreement processing in a business scenario.
Select and justify assignment urgency in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Assignment Ready defines when an assignment SLA starts: immediately, after a fixed delay, or at a DateTime property. Creation and readiness can differ. This setting applies to assignment SLAs; do not assume it delays every case-level deadline.

elements.text: Worked example: A settlement task is created at 10:00 but can start only at 16:00. Store today's settlement opening time in a DateTime property and start the assignment SLA then; a two-hour deadline is 18:00.

elements.description: GetNextWork uses assignment urgency. Assignment urgency combines the case contribution at assignment creation, assignment SLA increments and a manual assignment adjustment, capped at 100. A later manual change to case urgency does not retroactively update an existing assignment's case contribution.

elements.text: Worked example: A case contributes 20, the assignment SLA contributes 10 and a manual assignment adjustment contributes 5. The assignment priority is 35 before later SLA increments.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Creation is not readiness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Start the clock before the operator can work.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure Assignment Ready against the actual start requirement.

examPitfalls.title: Case versus assignment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing case urgency always updates every existing assignment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish case priority from the assignment's own SLA and adjustment.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A reconciliation assignment exists at noon but cannot be processed until a daily cut-off stored on the case. Which Assignment Ready configuration fits?

options.text: Dynamically defined on a DateTime property
A fixed delay regardless of the cut-off date
A case status field used as a duration

practiceQuiz.rationale: A DateTime property represents the actual opening time. A fixed delay cannot reliably model a variable cut-off; urgency controls priority rather than readiness.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The Case’s DateTime value supplies the actual readiness time.
optionExplanations.B: Urgency cannot replace the required wait until the cut-off.
optionExplanations.C: A constant duration cannot reliably follow a varying cut-off.
optionExplanations.D: A status label is not a scheduling DateTime or delay.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A task must wait exactly 45 minutes after creation before its SLA begins. Which configuration is simplest?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A timed delay shifts readiness. Goal and deadline intervals measure work after the SLA starts; they do not model a wait before it starts.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A goal measures elapsed work time; it does not postpone readiness.
optionExplanations.B: A deadline measures the interval after readiness, not the initial wait.
optionExplanations.C: Priority adjustment does not schedule the SLA start.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed 45-minute delay directly expresses the required wait.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An assignment becomes ready at 09:30 and its deadline is two hours after readiness. With no business-calendar adjustment, when is the deadline?

options.text: Two hours after case creation, regardless of readiness

practiceQuiz.rationale: The assignment SLA interval starts at readiness. This scenario explicitly excludes calendar adjustments.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The interval begins at assignment readiness in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: The deadline is time-based, not triggered by a stage transition.
optionExplanations.C: 09:30 plus two hours is 11:30, with calendar adjustment excluded.
optionExplanations.D: 09:30 is the start; the deadline is two hours later.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are supported ways to establish assignment readiness?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Readiness can be immediate, property-driven or delayed. Authorization records and labels do not schedule the assignment SLA.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A presentation label does not schedule readiness.
optionExplanations.B: A DateTime property can dynamically establish readiness.
optionExplanations.C: A timed delay defines the wait before readiness.
optionExplanations.D: An authorization role does not supply a readiness time.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A supervisor changes case urgency after an assignment was created. Why should the existing assignment's priority be checked separately?

options.text: Its case-urgency contribution was taken at assignment creation

practiceQuiz.rationale: Assignment SLA and assignment adjustments can change priority, but a later manual case urgency adjustment does not automatically replace the creation-time contribution.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The case contribution was captured when this assignment was created.
optionExplanations.B: SLA increments and assignment adjustments can still change urgency.
optionExplanations.C: A case urgency change does not delete existing assignments.
optionExplanations.D: GetNextWork uses assignment priority, including its other contributions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A case contributes 15, the assignment SLA contributes 20 and the assignment adjustment is 5. What urgency follows, before any cap is needed?
practiceQuiz.rationale: These three assignment-urgency components total 40. Counting only the SLA or case contribution omits part of the calculation.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: 15 omits both SLA and assignment adjustment.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which priority is used by GetNextWork to select the next eligible assignment?
practiceQuiz.rationale: GetNextWork prioritizes eligible assignments using assignment urgency. This is distinct from application metadata.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A label identifies the Case Type, not its assignment priority.
optionExplanations.B: Patch versions select rule versions, not work priority.
optionExplanations.C: Assignment urgency prioritizes the eligible work candidates.
optionExplanations.D: A training quiz score has no GetNextWork role.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SLA escalation would raise assignment urgency beyond the supported range. Which upper bound should the design respect?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Urgency is bounded at 100. A higher number is not an unlimited priority mechanism; design escalation actions as well as increments.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The supported urgency range has a ceiling.
optionExplanations.B: 100 is the upper bound; larger adjustments are ignored.
optionExplanations.C: 70 is a valid value, not the ceiling.
